name: Diwali Bingo
description: A trivia game about the festival of Diwali, its legends, and rituals. Players answer questions to fill their bingo cards and win prizes.

questions.question: Which sage is credited with writing the original Sanskrit epic of the Ramayana?
questions.hint: He is also believed to have given shelter to Sita during her exile and raised Luv and Kush.

questions.question: Which saint-poet wrote the Awadhi version of the Ramayana called "Ramcharitmanas"?
questions.hint: His work is widely recited during Ramlila performances before Dussehra.

questions.question: Which sage trained young Rama and Lakshmana and later took them to protect his yagna from demons?
questions.hint: He also gave Rama a set of celestial weapons known as "Devastras."

questions.question: Who was the royal guru (kulguru) of the Ikshvaku dynasty and King Dasharatha's chief advisor?
questions.hint: This sage owned the divine wish-fulfilling cow Nandini and had a famous rivalry with Vishwamitra.

questions.question: Which sage, residing near Dandakaranya, gifted Rama a divine bow and quiver before his final battle?
questions.hint: He is also credited with confining two troublesome asuras, Vatapi and Ilvala, in the south.

questions.question: Which celestial sage first narrated the story of Rama to Valmiki, inspiring him to compose the epic?
questions.hint: This wandering sage carries a veena and often appears as a divine messenger in Hindu mythology.

questions.question: Who is the seventh avatar of Vishnu and the prince of Ayodhya at the center of the epic?
questions.hint: His triumphant return from exile is the reason Diwali is celebrated with rows of lamps.

questions.question: Which princess was discovered in a furrow of a ploughed field and later became Rama's wife?
questions.hint: She proved her purity by walking through fire — the Agni Pariksha — in Lanka.

questions.question: Which brother chose to accompany Rama into 14 years of exile instead of staying in the palace?
questions.hint: He is often shown standing guard beside Rama and Sita in temple idols.

questions.question: Which queen demanded two boons that led to Rama's banishment and her own son's coronation?
questions.hint: Her maid convinced her to make this fateful request.

questions.question: Which goddess of wealth and prosperity is worshipped in homes on the main night of Diwali?
questions.hint: She is said to visit only clean, well-lit homes on the darkest night of the month.

questions.question: Which king of Mithila found baby Sita in a field and later hosted her wedding to Rama?
questions.hint: He was ploughing a field when he discovered the infant girl.

questions.question: Which brother refused the throne and ruled Ayodhya by placing Rama's sandals on it instead?
questions.hint: He lived austerely in the village of Nandigram during Rama's exile.

questions.question: Which vanara king was killed by Rama with a single arrow from behind a tree, to help his rival reclaim a kingdom?
questions.hint: His death came during a duel with his own brother over a throne and a wife.

questions.question: Which of Lakshmana's wife is said, in folklore, to have slept for 14 years so he wouldn't have to?
questions.hint: This let him stay awake guarding Rama and Sita throughout their exile.

questions.question: Which of Rama and Sita's twin sons was raised by Valmiki and later reunited his parents at a horse sacrifice?
questions.hint: He shares his name with a fragrant grass used in a well-known Ayurvedic remedy.

questions.question: Which twin son of Rama, alongside his brother, challenged Rama's own army during the Ashwamedha Yagna?
questions.hint: A South Indian city and a valley in Kashmir are named after him.

questions.question: Which king of Ayodhya died of a broken heart after banishing his beloved son to the forest?
questions.hint: He once accidentally killed a boy while hunting by sound alone, a curse that foretold his sorrow.

questions.question: Which ten-headed king of Lanka abducted Sita, leading to a great war?
questions.hint: Effigies of him are burned across India on Dussehra.

questions.question: Which giant brother of Ravana slept for six months at a stretch and was famous for his enormous appetite?
questions.hint: He was woken up and killed by Rama during the war, despite being a devoted brother.

questions.question: Which of Ravana's brothers defected to Rama's side, revealing Lanka's secrets, and was later crowned king there?
questions.hint: He is remembered as a symbol of righteousness triumphing over blood loyalty.

questions.question: Which demoness's mocking of Sita and infatuation with Rama set the abduction plot in motion?
questions.hint: Her nose and ears were cut off by Lakshmana after she attacked Sita.

questions.question: Which son of Ravana used illusion in battle and was finally slain by Lakshmana?
questions.hint: His name means "one who cries like thunder," a cry he let out at birth.

questions.question: Which hunchbacked palace maid convinced Queen Kaikeyi to ask for Rama's exile?
questions.hint: She feared losing her influence in the palace if Rama became king.

questions.question: Which fearsome demoness of Dandakaranya forest was killed by Rama at his guru's request, despite being female?
questions.hint: A village near modern-day Delhi is believed to take its name from her domain.

questions.question: Which of Ravana's generals led the demon army and was killed by Lakshmana during the war for Lanka?
questions.hint: He was sent as an emissary to the monkey army's camp before the war began.

questions.question: Which vanara deity flew across the ocean to find Sita and later burned Lanka with his tail?
questions.hint: He is worshipped as the embodiment of devotion and strength, son of the wind god.

questions.question: Which elephant-headed deity is worshipped alongside Lakshmi on Diwali night for wisdom and new beginnings?
questions.hint: He is invoked at the start of most Hindu rituals as the remover of obstacles.

questions.question: Which demon disguised himself as a golden deer to lure Rama away so Sita could be abducted?
questions.hint: He had earlier tried to disrupt Vishwamitra's yagna alongside another demon, Subahu.

questions.question: Which vulture king sacrificed his life fighting Ravana to try to save Sita?
questions.hint: He was an old friend of King Dasharatha and lived long enough to tell Rama what happened.

questions.question: Which vanara, one of two architect brothers, helped design the floating bridge to Lanka, blessed so that stones wouldn't sink for him?
questions.hint: He and his brother were sons of the celestial architect Vishwakarma.

questions.question: Which vanara, brother to the builder of Ram Setu, also worked alongside him to construct the bridge to Lanka?
questions.hint: Together with his brother, every stone he touched floated instead of sinking.

questions.question: Which vanara king, restored to his throne by Rama, commanded the monkey army in the search for Sita?
questions.hint: He had been hiding in fear of his own brother before Rama helped him reclaim his kingdom.

questions.question: Which ancient bear king joined Rama's army as the oldest and wisest of the animal chiefs?
questions.hint: He claimed to have witnessed the churning of the ocean, the Samudra Manthan, in his youth.

questions.question: In which capital city did Rama rule, and to which he returned in triumph, prompting the first Diwali celebrations?
questions.hint: This city on the banks of the Sarayu is considered one of Hinduism's seven holiest cities.

questions.question: Which island kingdom, ruled by Ravana, was said to be built entirely of gold?
questions.hint: Rama's army built a bridge across the sea to reach this kingdom.

questions.question: What is the name of the bridge believed to have been built across the sea to Lanka, still visible in satellite images today?
questions.hint: It's also known as Adam's Bridge, stretching between India and Sri Lanka.

questions.question: In which garden was Sita held captive in Lanka, guarded by demonesses, while awaiting rescue?
questions.hint: Hanuman first met Sita here after leaping across the ocean.

questions.question: In which vast forest did Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana spend most of their 14-year exile?
questions.hint: This forest spanned the region south of the Vindhya mountains.

questions.question: On the banks of which river does Ayodhya sit, the same river Rama is believed to have entered when he finally left the mortal world?
questions.hint: This river is a tributary of the Ganga in present-day Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: What are the small oil lamps lit in rows outside homes to welcome Lakshmi on Diwali night?
questions.hint: The festival's name, "Deepavali," literally means "a row of these."

questions.question: What colorful floor art, made from powders, flowers, or rice, is drawn at doorways during Diwali to welcome guests and deities?
questions.hint: Its intricate patterns are often geometric or floral and symmetrical.

questions.question: What is the name of the magical herb Hanuman fetched from a Himalayan mountain to revive Lakshmana?
questions.hint: Unable to identify it, Hanuman carried the entire mountain it grew on instead.

questions.question: What is the name of Lord Shiva's divine bow that Rama broke to win Sita's hand in marriage?
questions.hint: Breaking this bow at Sita's swayamvar was the test set by King Janaka.

questions.question: What is the name of the flying chariot, once belonging to Kubera before Ravana seized it, which Rama used to fly home to Ayodhya?
questions.hint: This aerial vehicle could expand or shrink to fit any number of passengers.

questions.question: What is the name of the supremely destructive celestial weapon Rama used to finally kill Ravana?
questions.hint: Associated with Brahma, this weapon was also infamously used at the end of the Mahabharata war.

questions.question: What is the name of the festival marking Rama's victory over Ravana, celebrated with the burning of effigies?
questions.hint: It falls on the tenth day of Navratri, marking the "victory of good over evil."

questions.question: In which Hindu lunar month, roughly falling in October–November, is Diwali celebrated?
questions.hint: This month also hosts the holy river-dip festival of Purnima at its end.

questions.question: On which type of moon night — with no moon visible at all — is the main Diwali Lakshmi Puja celebrated?
questions.hint: Its total darkness is exactly why rows of lamps are needed to light up the night.

questions.question: What is the festival celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters, observed two days after the main Diwali night?
questions.hint: Legend ties it to Yama visiting his sister, after whom a river is also named.

questions.question: What celebration, observed the day after Diwali, honors a mountain associated with Krishna lifting it to shelter villagers from Indra's storm?
questions.hint: Devotees build small replicas of this hill using cow dung or food offerings called "Annakut."
